N-2.1-A.skill: apply Newton's second law to a chosen system: internal force pairs cancel, so only external forces set the acceleration of the center of mass

N-2.1-B.skill: locate the center of mass at a later time: it moves at the mass-weighted velocity even when the parts move differently

N-2.2-A.skill: draw forces by their physical sources: a thrown object keeps no "force of the throw", and drag opposes the velocity

N-2.2-B.skill: analyze a free-body diagram of a hanging object: balance horizontal and vertical components to find unequal cable tensions

N-2.3-A.skill: combine Newton's second and third laws: the contact force between two pushed blocks is found from the acceleration of the block being pushed

N-2.3-B.skill: keep third-law pairs distinct from balanced forces: contact forces stay equal and opposite even when the surface and object accelerate

N-2.4-A.skill: use constant velocity (net force zero) to find an unknown force by vector balance, not by assuming constant velocity needs a force

N-2.4-B.skill: link motion to the net force: constant velocity means balanced forces in any direction, and speeding up or slowing down changes the tension from the weight

N-2.5-A.skill: apply Newton's second law separately to connected objects to find the tension, which is not simply the weight of the hanging mass

N-2.5-B.skill: compare accelerations in opposite directions of travel when a resistive force reverses direction with the velocity

N-2.6-A.skill: find where the net gravitational force from two masses cancels, using the inverse-square dependence rather than a simple ratio of masses

N-2.6-B.skill: compare gravitational forces and accelerations of two bodies: equal forces give accelerations inversely proportional to mass

N-2.7-A.skill: find kinetic friction when the applied force has a vertical component that changes the normal force

N-2.7-B.skill: use static friction as a supporting force: the normal force comes from the pushing force, not the weight, when a block is held against a wall

N-2.8-A.skill: extract the spring constant and the natural length from two force-length readings, where the length is not the stretch

N-2.8-B.skill: combine springs: the same force passes through springs in series so their stretches add, while parallel springs share the load with a common stretch

N-2.9-A.skill: use friction as the centripetal force on a flat curve: the maximum speed does not depend on mass

N-2.9-B.skill: scale the centripetal force with speed and radius together using F proportional to v²/r
